findings.title: Single primary with no streaming replica
findings.detail: pg_stat_replication returned no rows and the server is not in recovery, so a host failure means downtime until a restore completes.
findings.recommendation: Add a hot standby (streaming replication with a replication slot) and a tested promotion procedure; decide the target recovery time with the business first.

findings.title: WAL archiving is off
findings.detail: archive_mode is off, so point in time recovery is not possible from this server; recovery is limited to the last full backup taken by external tooling.
findings.recommendation: Enable archive_mode with an archive_command or a backup tool that manages WAL (pgBackRest, Barman, or the cloud provider's PITR), then run a timed restore test.

findings.title: No schema migration history table found
findings.detail: None of the common migration tools (Flyway, Liquibase, Alembic, Django, Prisma, Knex, goose, EF) left a history table, so schema changes are probably applied by hand.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one migration tool and put every DDL change in version control with a review step; start by baselining the current schema.

findings.title: DDL is not logged
findings.detail: log_statement is none and there are no event triggers, so there is no record of who changed the schema and when.
findings.recommendation: Set log_statement to ddl (no restart needed) so every schema change lands in the server log.

findings.title: Login roles have no password expiry
findings.detail: 2 login role(s) have no VALID UNTIL date: discovery, importer.
findings.recommendation: Decide a rotation period for human accounts and set VALID UNTIL; keep service accounts on vault managed rotation.

findings.title: 2 index(es) have never been scanned
findings.detail: Indexes with zero scans since statistics reset cost write time and disk: orders_status_idx (16 kB), ix_import_runs_hash (16 kB).
findings.recommendation: Confirm the statistics window covers a full business cycle, then drop the unused ones with DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY.

findings.title: pg_stat_statements is not installed
findings.detail: Without it there is no per query view of time, calls and I/O, so slow query work is guesswork.
findings.recommendation: Add pg_stat_statements to shared_preload_libraries (restart) and CREATE EXTENSION it in each database.

findings.title: Slow statements are not logged
findings.detail: log_min_duration_statement is `-1`, so no statement is ever written to the log by duration.
findings.recommendation: Set log_min_duration_statement to a value such as 1000 ms (no restart) and review the log weekly.

findings.title: track_io_timing is off
findings.detail: I/O time per query is not recorded, which removes a cheap diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Set track_io_timing to on; the cost is negligible on modern hardware.

findings.title: log_lock_waits is off
findings.detail: lock waits over deadlock_timeout are not logged, which removes a cheap diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Set log_lock_waits to on; the cost is negligible on modern hardware.

findings.title: Server log relies on the service wrapper
findings.detail: logging_collector is off and log_destination is not syslog; on Debian and Ubuntu packages the cluster wrapper captures stderr into /var/log/postgresql, on other installs the lines may be lost.
findings.recommendation: Confirm where the log lands and that it rotates; otherwise enable logging_collector with daily rotation or route to syslog or the cloud log service.

findings.title: 1 table(s) have no primary key
findings.detail: Tables without a primary key cannot be logically replicated by default and make upserts and deduplication awkward: public.audit_log.
findings.recommendation: Add a surrogate or natural primary key to each, starting with the largest.

unknowns.question: Backup schedule, retention and the date of the last successful restore test
unknowns.how_to_obtain: Ask the operations owner for the backup job definition, retention policy and restore test log; the database cannot report these
